There's a New Kind of Lifted Ram Truck in Town, 1776 Off-Road Is Born in Texas
28 photos
Photo: 1776
With so many custom garages taking care of Americans' appetite for modified vehicles, you'd think the market is saturated, and there's little room for newcomers to come in and play the game. Think again, as the Hennessey Group thinks quite the opposite.
Out of the blue, the behemoth that also happens to own Hennessey Performance , the makers of the $2.5 Blackbird, among other things, announced the launch of something called the 1776 Off-Road. That would be the makers of upgrades of all shapes and sizes for the likes of the Ram 1500 and Ram 2500 pickup trucks.
To make sure everybody notices the newcomer's arrival on the national market, the Texas-based crew also released the initial details of some specially prepped pickup trucks from the above-mentioned families, and let me tell you, they are quite something to behold.
The trucks were born after they've been fitted with 1776's first two customization packages. And I'll start with the smaller of the two, which is at the same time my favorite one of the pair.
Photo: 1776 The 1776 Off-Road comes along with whatever powertrain customers choose off the factory floor, and many of the stock components as well, but adds on top of everything a lot of extras to make it meaner and more capable.
The customizer included in the package, first and foremost, new hardware for translating more effectively the engine's power into forward or backward motion, regardless of the terrain it travels over. We've got, thus, 22-inch off-road wheels fitted with 35-inch all-terrain tires and tied to a completely new off-road suspension system. There's also a lift at play, with six inches of extra ground clearance gained this way on both ends.
For the truck's powertrain, 1776 provides a stainless cat-back exhaust system with black tips. For easier access, the sides of the 1500 are now fitted with power running boards. Visual enhancements include painted off-road fender flares, while the front displays a grille-mounted LED light bar. The bedside is decorated as well, in this case with a special Stars & Stripes vinyl livery.
The interior was not left to chance either, with WeatherTech front and rear floor liners matching diamond-quilted leather and Alcantara seats and an interior console plaque being installed.
Photo: 1776 The bigger Ram 2500 can be upgraded over at 1776 as well, and it too becomes even meaner by throwing into the battle even more aftermarket hardware. It all starts, just like in the case of the 1500, underneath the bodywork.
This truck rides on a BDS four-inch suspension system at the front and BDS 2.5-inch coil springs at the rear. The setup includes high-clearance tubular radius arms, performance shock absorbers, and a dual steering stabilizer, and it too is connected to 22-inch off-road wheels on all corners, this time shod in larger, 37-inch all-terrain tires. The custom crew opted to include a performance exhaust tip in the package.
From here onward, there are a lot of similarities with the solutions offered for the 1500: color-matched fender flares, LED off-road light pods mounted on the A-pillar, WeatherTech front and rear floor liners inside, diamond-quilted leather and Alcantara seats, and an interior console-mounted plaque, among others. Why, there are even the same raised exterior badges.
1776 says it offers both packages complete with a three-year, 36,000-mile (58,000 km) bumper-to-bumper warranty, but makes no mention of how much each of the packages is worth in this exact form. Not even the company's website, already up and running, is more revealing in that respect.
Photo: 1776 No matter how much 1776 will charge for these upgrades, it's important to note that every single sale will be matched with a donation of undisclosed size made to the Folds of Honor, a charity that provides educational scholarships to wives and kids of fallen or disabled soldiers and first responders.
The two packages designed for the two Ram trucks are, according to 1776, only the beginning, as more will follow in the not-so-distant future, and they'll cover pickups made by other companies as well, Ford and GM. I'll keep an eye on that, as I can't wait to see what their trucks will look like with such things on.
As for where you'll find these upgrades, the company website I mentioned earlier is not the only way to go. The 1776 packages and upgrades will be sold through participating Ram dealers, but you’ll have to check if your local one made the cut.
Hennessey hopes the newly-founded customization company will live and and thrive in this segment, and it's probably not wrong. Americans not only buy pickup trucks like there's no tomorrow, but a large chunk of them also decide what the factory offers is not enough, so they turn to customizers the likes of 1776. As for the choice of name made for this new crew, I think it needs little introduction, especially this year.
